text: What is published here? Agent Skills only: portable SKILL.md instructions plus optional flat resources and closed marketplace metadata. Hooks, MCP servers, custom agents, and automatically executable extension types are not supported by this MVP. Does “Marketplace reviewed” mean safe? No. It means named reviewers assessed the exact published revision, digest, declared capabilities, and available evidence. The marketplace does not use “safe” or “verified secure” claims. What does “Auto-checked” mean? The exact package bytes passed the automated policy and content scan at the published revision. Community packages publish at this tier; no human review is claimed. Each record also shows an access level derived from its declared capabilities. What does “Unreviewed candidate” mean? An immutable third-party source was submitted for review. Trusted CI still needs to compute its digest and run deterministic policy checks, and BC Gov reviewers have not approved it. Why is the source a full commit SHA? A branch or tag can move. A full commit SHA plus package-tree digest binds discovery, scan, review, install, and receipt evidence to the same bytes. Why are there two companion skills? bcgov-find-extension handles discovery, controlled installation, and third-party candidate registration. bcgov-create-extension handles authoring and hosted submission. Keeping the entry points separate loads only the workflow needed for the request. Are installed skills global too? Reviewed catalog skills default to the current project. Third-party candidates are project-local only. The finder shows the exact destination and material capabilities before confirmation. Where is installation evidence? Preferred APM installs use apm.yml and apm.lock.yaml ; the fallback installer may write skills-lock.json . Legacy helper receipts live under .github/agent-marketplace/receipts/ . Local evidence stays in the project unless the developer chooses to share it for support or incident response. Can a companion publish its own work? No. The creator may open a signed draft pull request, but cannot approve, merge, modify protection, or assign review status. CI and human reviewers decide publication. What if I cannot push a branch? The creator preserves the staged package and provides an access-request action. Fork PRs are intentionally blocked. Third-party registration uses issues and does not require branch access. How is a package quarantined? Maintainers set its lifecycle to quarantined , regenerate, and publish through review. The finder excludes it from default results. Support then identifies affected receipts or declared dependencies and publishes update or removal guidance. See the operations runbook and the private reporting route . text: i Development preview. The companion install command below installs immutable bytes from a pinned pre-release revision ( 2046da7b0de0f673bf39208b35385c1516be4c75 ). Content is validated, but this release is not final. Install the two companions once per device with the -g (global) flag so they are available in every workspace, not just the current project. APM is preferred because it records a manifest and lockfile: apm install -g \ bcgov/agent-marketplace/skills/community/bcgov-find-extension#catalog-2026.10.01 \ bcgov/agent-marketplace/skills/community/bcgov-create-extension#catalog-2026.10.01 \ --target copilot The -g flag installs to your user scope ( ~/.apm/ ) instead of the current project, so you run this once rather than in every repository. If APM is unavailable, use the catalog-pinned Skills CLI: npx skills@1.5.23 add \ https://github.com/bcgov/agent-marketplace/tree/catalog-2026.10.01 \ --skill bcgov-find-extension --skill bcgov-create-extension \ --agent github-copilot -y

text: Only these keys are accepted (any other key is rejected by the validator): name , description , owner , tags , license , allowed-tools , compatibility , metadata . text: After the frontmatter, the body MUST contain — in this order — an H1 title followed by all seven ## sections. When a skill needs deeper material — long procedures, lookup tables, worked examples, API detail — put it in a references/ file the agent pulls on demand, and link it from the ## References section.

sectionTitle: Keep bundled resources flat: one level deep
text: Skills may ship scripts/ , references/ , and assets/ directories beside the SKILL.md . These must stay exactly one level deep : flat files only, no nested subdirectories. Use references/REFERENCE.md , not references/api/v1/REFERENCE.md . A flat layout keeps on-demand resources predictable for the agent to locate.

text: For each changed skill, the validator confirms all of the following. If this list and the validator script ( scripts/validate_skill.py ) ever disagree, the script wins. If you see a failure on a PR, this list maps directly to the checks: The SKILL.md starts with a closed YAML frontmatter block that parses as a mapping. name and description are present and non-empty. name is kebab-case, at most 64 characters, and matches the skill's directory name . description is at most 1024 characters and contains no angle brackets. No unexpected frontmatter keys are present (only name , description , owner , tags , license , allowed-tools , compatibility , metadata ). The body has an H1 title. All seven required sections are present: Use When , Don't Use When , Workflow , Rules , Examples , Edge Cases , References . None of those required sections is empty. The whole SKILL.md is at most 500 lines. Any bundled scripts/ , references/ , or assets/ directory is flat (no nested subdirectories). No cross-skill duplicates. When more than one skill is being validated, the check refuses two skills sharing the same name , the same description , or the same normalised body (the part after the H1 title and one-line summary). Catches copy-pasted manifests before they ship. Skip with --no-duplicates when you intentionally want to compare a single file.

sectionTitle: Gotchas the validator can't always pinpoint
text: Colons inside description . YAML treats key: value as a mapping. If your description contains : (colon + space) — e.g. "Use when: planning a deployment" — wrap the whole value in single quotes so PyYAML doesn't try to split it. Double quotes also work but then you have to escape any literal " . Section headings use a straight ASCII apostrophe. Write ## Don't Use When with ' (U+0027), not the curly ' (U+2019) that some editors auto-insert. The validator normalises smart quotes to straight in the heading-match step, so the canonical form in your file is the ASCII one.
